note: Requirement IDs are transcribed verbatim from the FRD. Do NOT renumber them to suit a test file — tag the test with the requirement's real ID instead. `layer` records where a requirement can honestly be proven: 'api' for contract/business behaviour, 'ui' for anything only a browser can show, 'client' for device-native behaviour no automated bench can reach.

requirements.text: A rescheduled Kall retains a clear Scheduled vs Rescheduled status distinction.
The Subject field is present on every message regardless of recipient count.
The available action set differs by role: sender actions vs recipient actions.
An edited message retains a visible edit indicator; a recalled message is removed entirely.
Read-receipt data is recorded for every mail sent, matching Katchup's behaviour.
An account must complete activation before its first successful login.
Identifier uniqueness is enforced at submission, not deferred to activation.
Read receipts are consistent across Katchup and KMail.
Account, password and acceptable-use rules apply uniformly at account creation.
Create a scheduled Kall with a title, date, and start/end time.
Add one or more participants to a scheduled Kall.
Reschedule a previously scheduled Kall, updating its date and time.
Update the status tag of a rescheduled Kall and retain the original entry's identity.
Place a direct call to a contact.
Call external contacts from the device's native phone book.
Display a contacts screen showing the current contact count.
Maintain a call log showing participant names, roles/teams and duration.
Record exact start and end timestamps for each call in the call log.
Start a new message including a Subject field alongside the body.
Require the Subject field to be populated before a message can be sent.
Attach one or more files to a message.
Add Copy (Cc) recipients to a message.
Add Confidential Copy recipients, hidden from other recipients.
Support group messaging to multiple recipients as a group.
Record and display a read receipt per recipient, with exact open date/time.
Allow the sender to Edit a previously sent message.
Display an "Edited:" label on any message edited after sending.
Allow the sender to Recall a sent message, removing it from the recipient's view.
Allow the sender to Recall and Repost an edited message as one action.
Allow the sender to attach a Note to a sent message.
Allow the sender to set a Reminder on a sent message.
Allow the sender to Transfer a sent message to another recipient.
Allow the sender to Forward a sent message.
Allow the sender to Forward a sent message with its full thread.
Allow the sender to Copy a sent message's content.
Allow the sender to Save a sent message.
Support Text-to-Speech playback of a message's content.
Allow the sender to Delete a sent message.
Allow a recipient to Reply to a received message.
Allow a recipient to add a Comment on a received message.
Allow a recipient to request Clarification on a received message.
Allow a recipient to Report a Message.
Present a More Options entry last in the received-message action list.
Compose and send a new mail message.
Add one or more recipients to a mail message.
Attach one or more files to a mail message.
Record and display a read receipt per mail, with exact open date/time.
Open a mail in another installed mail application via an open-with sheet.
Add external (non-KPOST) email recipients to a message.
Transfer or Share a message to Gmail.
Transfer or Share a message to Outlook.
Transfer or Share a message to Yahoo Mail.
Present a registration form capturing the required user details.
Validate all required registration fields before allowing submission.
Reject registration using an email/identifier already associated with an account.
Enforce password-strength rules at account creation.
Require acceptance of the terms of use before completing registration.
Require account activation as a distinct step before first login.
Send an activation prompt on successful registration.
Reject login for an account that has not completed activation.
Allow a registered, activated user to log in with their credentials.
Reject login with incorrect credentials and present an appropriate error.
Maintain an authenticated session following successful login.
Allow a logged-in user to log out, terminating the active session.
Message send latency supports real-time conversational use.
Read-receipt recording introduces no perceptible delay in delivery.
The Auth Service is available for all login and session-validation operations.
Message and mail delivery degrade gracefully rather than losing data silently.
The platform supports account growth without user migration or re-registration.
All authenticated operations require a valid JWT issued by the Auth Service.
Confidential Copy recipients are not visible to other recipients.
Account passwords are subject to enforced strength rules at creation.
Framework, ORM and database internals are never exposed in a response body.
The recipient of a platform notification is derived from the record, never chosen by the caller.
An identifier supplied in a request body or query never overrides the identity carried on the token.
User-supplied content is stored and served escaped; submitted markup is never returned as executable script.
Read-receipt information is presented so an end user can interpret it unaided.
